headline: Mostly dry, mild weather through Friday, then light weekend showers, a mostly dry week, and a possible wetter pattern by early November.
summary: Western Washington stays mostly dry and mild through Friday. Thursday's weakening front left cloudy skies, and Friday should be clearer and a bit cooler, with low clouds and fog likely early Friday morning, especially south of Puget Sound and over the Kitsap Peninsula, clearing by afternoon. A low pressure system moving toward Washington from the north brings a chance of showers on Saturday. Most of the rain should fall along the Olympic Peninsula, while inland areas through Puget Sound get only a few hundredths of an inch. Some showers may linger into Sunday under mostly cloudy skies, again with only a few hundredths of an inch, and conditions turn drier by Sunday afternoon. Saturday morning lows should be in the upper 30s to low 40s, and mountain valleys could dip into the low 30s, so frost or a light freeze is possible there. The rest of next week looks mostly dry, though forecasters are less sure of the low's track early next week: some model runs send it into Oregon, keeping things cooler and cloudier, while others bring weak high pressure. Looking further out, there are early hints of a more active pattern around the end of October and the first week of November, with a slight risk of heavy rain, possible mountain snow, and breezier conditions on the immediate coast. Those are early signals, not firm predictions. Small Craft Advisories for the Pacific coastal waters run until Friday morning and afternoon because of strong northwest winds and rough seas, which mainly affects mariners. There are no watches, warnings, or advisories for land areas.
changes: Early-morning discussions described an uncertain, possibly wetter weekend with rain chances lasting into Monday. By afternoon and night, forecasters said weekend rain would be light, mostly on the Olympic Peninsula, ending Sunday afternoon with a mostly dry week after. They also added Friday morning fog, possible frost in mountain valleys Saturday, and a possible wetter pattern in early November.
